inventory.notes: When the pref is non-empty the OS voice registry is never consulted, so the list replaces the real voices instead of overriding them. The NAME|LANG|D|L parsing and the stealth-voice: URI construction live in Mozilla code; move them to our file behind one call. Synthetic voices are never registered with the OS. [verified: CONFIRMED functional gap, not a crash: SpeakUtterance passes voice->GetVoiceURI() (nsSynthVoiceRegistry.cpp:633) to FindBestMatch, which looks it up in mUriVoiceMap (:574-580) and, finding nothing, falls back to a voice chosen by language or default (:582-622). The utterance is spoken with an OS voice other than the one the page selected.]

verifier.why: Voice-resolution risk checked in nsSynthVoiceRegistry.cpp: speaking with a stealth voice does not fail but silently falls back to a language/default voice.

inventory.anchor: file-scope IsStealthVoiceURI and GetStealthVoiceField (new, top of file); SpeechSynthesisVoice::GetVoiceURI, GetName, GetLang, LocalService, Default
inventory.notes: The accessors each have a 2-4 line prefix that is already a hook. The parser (about 25 lines) and the GetVoiceURI rewrite (about 8 lines) should move to our file. GetVoiceURI now returns the urn:moz-tts:sapi: scheme on every platform, including Linux and macOS builds, by design (per the comment). The GetVoiceURI comment is a long Italian narrative with measurement dates; translate and trim it, or move it out of the Mozilla file. The comment also names a voice ('Microsoft David') and a product. [verified: the rewritten urn:moz-tts:sapi: string is what SpeakUtterance sends to the parent (nsSynthVoiceRegistry.cpp:633), where FindBestMatch cannot match it in mUriVoiceMap (:574-580) and falls back to a language/default voice.]
